other.model: Tukey biweight robust linear regression (statsmodels RLM)
other.formula: log_wage_gain ~ C(edu_group, Treatment(reference="college_degree")) + C(country) + C(sex) + age_home_job + age_home_job_sq + yearLastHomeJob + yearLastUsJob + C(occGroupLastHomeJob)

result_raw.result_text: In the adjusted Tukey biweight robust regression, immigrants with no high-school exposure had higher log wage gains than immigrants with college degrees; the estimated log-point difference was 0.2745, corresponding to about a 31.6% proportional difference.

conclusion.rule_applied: Support requires the no-high-school minus college-degree coefficient to be positive, because the focal claim expects larger wage gains for immigrants with no high-school exposure than for immigrants with a college degree. For coefficient-based frequentist results, p < 0.05 indicates strong support, while a positive estimate with p >= 0.05 would still be weak directional support. Opposite requires affirmative statistically supported evidence in the contrary direction.
conclusion.uncertainty_statement: The estimate is positive and statistically significant under the normal approximation, with p = 0.000459 and a 95% confidence interval excluding zero in the expected direction, so the evidence is strong.
conclusion.conclusion_text: Task1 supports the focal claim: the adjusted robust-regression estimate indicates larger wage gains for immigrants with no high-school exposure than for immigrants with college degrees.
